title: Cubby Fundamentals
description: Cubby, the software Greens runs its storage sites on: where things live, how a lead becomes a reservation and a move-in, how a tenant ledger works with eight worked examples, taking payments and handling failed autopay, waives, credits and refunds, transfers and move-outs, the delinquency steps Cubby runs for Greens, gate codes, notes and tasks, and the open and close routine with its reports. Course 4 of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: What Cubby is, where things live, and Greens' five Cubby sites
How a lead becomes a reservation and a move-in
How a tenant ledger works: charges, payments, waives, credits, prepaid and the paid-through date
Eight worked ledger examples with the arithmetic, on Greens' first-of-month billing and jump day 26
Taking payments, autopay and the failed autopay call
Waives, credits, refunds, transfers and move-outs
The delinquency steps Cubby runs: overlock, lockout, liens and exemptions
Gate codes, notes, tasks, and the reports to run at open and close

questions.q: How do all five Greens Cubby sites bill rent?
options: On the 1st of the month, with jump day 26
questions.explanation: Every Greens site bills on the first of the month with a jump day of 26 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). Rent is due on the 1st whatever day the tenant moved in.

questions.q: A customer moves in on 11/27 at a Greens site. What rent do they pay at move-in?
options: The rest of November plus all of December
A full month, then again on 12/27
questions.explanation: A move-in on or after jump day 26 pays the days left in this month plus the whole next month, so the first regular bill is 01/01, not a few days later.

questions.q: In Cubby, what is a pricing group?
options: The unit type: units of one kind and size sharing one set of rates
A group of tenants who pay together
A report of rent by site
questions.explanation: A pricing group is the unit type, such as "10' x 10' Storage - Interior, Lower", with its street, web and walk-in rates.

questions.q: Cubby has a public online help center you can search for click-by-click instructions.
questions.explanation: Cubby has no public help center. Use the Cubby How-To pages, then your manager, then Cubby support through Greens' customer success manager.

questions.q: The Cubby Home page shows a count of document issues. What does it mean?
options: Leases whose paperwork is not complete, such as an unsigned lease or missing ID
questions.explanation: Document issues are leases with incomplete paperwork: lease agreement, ID, vehicle details or proof of insurance. Most leases brought over from the old system show incomplete documents (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: A caller asks about a parking space but will not rent today. What do you do in Cubby?
options: Create a lead with the real source, the rate quoted, a status and a follow-up task
Reserve a space for them anyway
Write their number on a sticky note
questions.explanation: Every caller or walk-in who does not rent today becomes a lead with a real source (not Other), the rate you quoted, a status, and a task for the follow-up you promised.

questions.q: What reservation fee does Greens charge?
questions.explanation: Greens charges no reservation fee (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). The $25.00 Administration Fee is charged at move-in, not at reservation.

questions.q: A new parking tenant is about to leave the counter. Which must be done in Cubby first? Choose all that apply.
options: Vehicle plate, state and type entered
questions.explanation: Nothing should leave the counter incomplete: signed lease, ID, vehicle details and a working gate code. New Greens move-ins pay no deposit (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Rent is $120.00 a month. A tenant moves in on 11/21 (November has 30 days). Using rent x days used / days in the month, what is the prorated rent?
questions.explanation: 11/21 through 11/30 is 10 days. 120.00 x 10 / 30 = $40.00. Always check the formula against a real Preview Charges.

questions.q: Rent is $120.00 a month, no protection plan. A tenant moves in on 11/28. What is due at move-in, including the $25.00 Administration Fee?
questions.explanation: 11/28 is on or after jump day 26: 3 days of November (120.00 x 3 / 30 = $12.00) plus December ($120.00) plus the $25.00 admin fee = $157.00.

questions.q: December rent of $150.00 and protection of $9.00 posted on 12/01. On 12/04 the tenant pays $100.00. How much rent is still open?
questions.explanation: Charges posted together are paid rent before insurance, so the $100.00 goes to rent: 150.00 - 100.00 = $50.00 of rent open, plus the $9.00 protection.

questions.q: An enclosed unit rents for $90.00 a month. Rent is unpaid on the 11th. What CA Late Fee does Cubby post?
questions.explanation: Greens' late fee for rent over $60 and under $100 is $15.00 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). 15% applies only from $100 of rent.

questions.q: A unit rents for $200.00 a month. What CA Late Fee posts on the 11th if rent is unpaid?
questions.explanation: For rent of $100 or more the fee is the greater of $20.00 or 15% of rent. 15% of $200.00 is $30.00, which is more than $20.00.

questions.q: Rent $95.00 plus protection $9.00. The tenant is paid through 11/30 and pays $312.00 on 11/20. What is the prepaid balance after the 01/01 charges post?
questions.explanation: $312.00 becomes prepaid. Each month uses $104.00 (95 + 9): after 12/01, $208.00; after 01/01, $104.00. The paid-through date is then 01/31.

questions.q: A lease is paid through 10/31. Today is 11/16. How many days past due is it?
questions.explanation: Days past due = today minus the paid-through date, minus 1. 11/16 minus 10/31 is 16 days; minus 1 = 15.

questions.q: A unit rents for $150.00. Nothing is paid, and the late fee posts on the 11th. What is the balance after the fee posts?
Rent is $160.00 and the tenant has an example 5% discount. What is the net due for the month?
questions.explanation: The rent posts at $160.00 and the discount posts as its own line: 5% of $160.00 = $8.00. Net: 160.00 - 8.00 = $152.00.

questions.q: Today is 12/10. A November rent charge posted on 11/01 is still open. How old is it, and which aging bucket is it in?
questions.explanation: 11/01 to 12/01 is 30 days, plus 9 to 12/10 = 39 days, which is in the 30-60 bucket of Aged Receivables.

questions.q: What does a waive do on the ledger?
options: Cancels all or part of one specific charge, now
Holds money for the next bill
Sends money back to the card
Moves a balance to another lease
questions.explanation: A waive cancels all or part of a specific charge right away, and always needs a reason. A credit waits for the next bill; a refund sends money back.

questions.q: How is a credit different from a waive?
options: A credit lowers today's balance; a waive does not
A credit does not lower today's balance; Cubby uses it on the next recurring charges
questions.explanation: A credit is goodwill money held on the lease and used on the next rent, then coverage, then automatic fees. It never lowers today's balance. Greens does not use credits today.

questions.q: A declined card payment posts to the ledger as a failed payment line.
questions.explanation: A declined attempt posts nothing to the ledger. If a tenant says they paid and you see nothing, the card was most likely declined.

questions.q: Rent $129.00 and protection $9.00 posted together on the 1st. The tenant pays $100.00. What is still open?
questions.explanation: Charges posted at the same time are paid rent before insurance. The $100.00 pays rent down to $29.00, and the $9.00 protection stays open: $38.00 in all.

questions.q: Put these in the order Cubby pays charges that posted at the same time.
questions.explanation: Cubby pays oldest charge first. Charges posted at the same time go prepaid, deposit, rent, state tax, local tax, then insurance.

questions.q: A tenant paid through 11/30 prepays three months on 11/15. What is the paid-through date on 11/16?
questions.explanation: It stays 11/30: prepaid money does not move the paid-through date until the charges it pays actually post. It moves one month at a time from 12/01.

questions.q: A lease is paid through 10/31. Today is 11/20. How many days past due is it?
questions.explanation: Days past due = today minus the paid-through date, minus 1. 11/20 minus 10/31 = 20 days; minus 1 = 19.

questions.q: A parking space rents for $250.00. What CA Late Fee posts on the 11th if rent is unpaid?
questions.explanation: For rent of $100 or more the fee is the greater of $20.00 or 15% of rent. 15% of $250.00 = $37.50.

questions.q: A unit rents for $110.00. What CA Late Fee posts on the 11th if rent is unpaid?
questions.explanation: 15% of $110.00 is $16.50, which is less than $20.00, so the fee is the greater amount: $20.00.

questions.q: When does Cubby post Greens' late fee?
questions.explanation: The late fee posts at 12:00 AM on the 11th, after 10 full days unpaid (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). California allows it only after 10 days past due and if the agreement says so.

questions.q: You refund a $129.00 rent payment for rent the tenant still owes. What happens to the balance?
questions.explanation: A refund puts the money back on the lease as owed unless the charge is also waived (check on a real refund). Never refund a charge the tenant still owes.

questions.q: A tenant's bank payment comes back as returned after it looked paid. What does Cubby do?
options: Reopens the charges the payment had paid
questions.explanation: A returned bank payment is marked failed, which reopens the charges it paid. The balance is owed again; call the tenant.

questions.q: Rent is $90.00. A tenant moves in on 11/11 (November has 30 days). What is the prorated rent?
questions.explanation: 11/11 through 11/30 is 20 days. 90.00 x 20 / 30 = $60.00. Check against a real Preview Charges.

questions.q: Rent is $100.00, no protection plan. A tenant moves in on 11/26. What is due at move-in with the $25.00 Administration Fee?
questions.explanation: 11/26 is on jump day 26: 5 days of November (100.00 x 5 / 30 = $16.67) plus December $100.00 plus $25.00 = $141.67.

questions.q: Rent $120.00 with the $2,500 plan at $14.00. Move-in 11/15 (16 days left, November has 30). Prorating both, what is due with the $25.00 admin fee?
questions.explanation: 16 days: rent 120 x 16 / 30 = $64.00; plan 14 x 16 / 30 = $7.47; plus $25.00 = $96.47. Check whether the plan prorates on a real Preview Charges.

questions.q: Rent $200.00, no plan, paid through 11/30. The tenant prepays $600.00 on 11/10. What is the paid-through date after the 01/01 charge posts?
questions.explanation: Prepaid pays each month as its charge posts: 12/01 moves it to 12/31, 01/01 to 01/31. $200.00 of prepaid is left for February.

questions.q: A tenant's rent is $160.00 with a one-month 50% off promotion. How does the bill for that month look on the ledger?
options: Rent $160.00 and a discount line of -$80.00
questions.explanation: Discounts post as their own line (50% of $160.00 = -$80.00); the rent stays at its full $160.00. That is why a tenant's bill seems to double when a promotion ends.

questions.q: Today is 11/15. An October rent charge posted on 10/01 is still open. Which aging bucket is it in?
questions.explanation: 10/01 to 11/15 is 45 days, which is in the 30-60 bucket of Aged Receivables. Each open charge is aged on its own.

questions.q: Which of these can be waived in Cubby? Choose all that apply.
options: A tax charge on its own
questions.explanation: Rent, fee, damage, coverage and deposit charges can be waived. Tax is waived in proportion with its charge; taxes on their own and waives cannot be waived.

questions.q: Greens uses Cubby's goodwill credits today.
questions.explanation: No credits have been issued at Greens (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). A tenant owed something usually needs a waive of a specific charge, inside the waiver policy.

questions.q: What deposit does a new Greens move-in pay?
questions.explanation: New move-ins pay no deposit. Only some leases brought over from the old system at Fairfield carry one (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: What one-time fee is charged on a new storage or parking lease at Greens?
questions.explanation: The Administration Fee is $25.00 on storage and parking leases; mailboxes pay a $10.00 Mailbox Administration Fee instead (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Rent $134.00 is open. The tenant pays $100.00 on the 5th. What happens on the 11th if nothing else is paid?
questions.explanation: Only payment in full stops the steps. With $34.00 still open, the late fee posts on the 11th. Tell partial payers the full amount.

questions.q: A tenant's autopay was declined on the 1st. Which task appears on the 2nd?
questions.explanation: On the 2nd Cubby's workflow creates "2nd - Call Failed Autopay Tenants." Call every tenant on it that day and note each call.

questions.q: A payment shows as pending. What do you do?
options: Do not run it again; wait, check, and ask your manager if it stays pending
questions.explanation: Pending means the outcome is unknown. Running it again can charge the tenant twice.

questions.q: Put Greens' delinquency steps in order, earliest first.
options: Late fee posts and Cubby changes the gate code (what Cubby does today; under review with counsel)
CA Preliminary Lien Notice fee posts
questions.explanation: The 2nd, 6th, 11th, 15th, 20th and 30th (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). The lien notice follows on day 35. The full ladder is on Greens Delinquency Timeline.

questions.q: On what day does Cubby flag a delinquent unit Overlock Needed?
questions.explanation: Cubby flags Overlock Needed at 12:00 AM on the 20th and staff usually apply it the next day (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). The timing is under review with counsel.

questions.q: What posts on the 15th for a tenant still unpaid?
questions.explanation: The CA Preliminary Lien Notice fee of $25.00 posts on the 15th, after 14 days unpaid. The $35.00 CA Lien Notice comes around day 35 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: Cubby flags a unit Overlock Needed. What do you check before you put the overlock on?
options: That it is still unpaid, has no delinquency exemption, and is the right unit
That the tenant answered the phone
questions.explanation: A tenant may have paid overnight or be exempt. Check the lease, then the unit number twice, before any overlock.

questions.q: A tenant whose unit is overlocked pays in full. What do you do?
options: Leave the overlock until next month
Remove it the same day, mark it removed in Cubby and check the gate code
Wait for the tenant to ask
questions.explanation: On payment Cubby flags the overlock for removal. Take it off the same day, mark it removed, and make sure the tenant's gate code works.

questions.q: What can a delinquency exemption pause? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: An exemption can pause late fees, overlock (lifting one already on), lien eligibility and collection messages. Rent still posts.

questions.q: A tenant tells you he has been deployed on active military duty. Which exemption reason fits?
questions.explanation: Military Service. A lien may not be enforced on a servicemember on active duty, or within 90 days after, without a court order. Tell your manager the same day.

questions.q: A lease can carry two active delinquency exemptions at the same time.
questions.explanation: Cubby allows one active exemption per lease. Change or extend it rather than adding a second.

questions.q: What must every delinquency exemption have?
questions.explanation: Every exemption needs an end date. Set a task for the day before it ends so someone checks whether to extend or end it.

questions.q: Which leases appear in the Home page's "liens to initiate" count?
options: Active leases that owe money, are past the lien waiting period, are not exempt, and have no lien started
questions.explanation: All four must be true. An exempt lease, or one where a lien has already started, is not on the list.

questions.q: A boat tenant reaches day 61 unpaid. What is the next step?
options: The vehicle lien path: "61st - Vehicle Lien Filing/Tow Notice"
questions.explanation: Vehicles, boats and trailers never go to the unit auction. Day 61 raises the vehicle lien task, with the Vehicle Lien Fee of $350.00 (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026).

questions.q: You are about to start a lien and the notes say the tenant's spouse is on active duty. What do you do?
options: Stop and tell your manager the same day
questions.explanation: A tenant or spouse on active duty can have protection that blocks a lien without a court order. Stop and escalate.

questions.q: A tenant in the lien process pays half of what they owe. Does the process stop?
options: No, only payment in full stops it
Only if they pay in cash
questions.explanation: Payment goes to the oldest charges first; the lease stays past due. Only payment in full, including posted fees, stops the lien.

questions.q: Where do you find a tenant's paid-through date, gate code and coverage in Cubby?
questions.explanation: Almost everything about a rental lives on its lease: ledger, paid-through date, autopay, coverage, documents, gate code, vehicle, activity and notes.

questions.q: What does an Archived task mean?
questions.explanation: Archived means dismissed. Work that was done, even a call with no answer, is completed with a note.

questions.q: You make the "6th - Call Past Due Tenants" call and nobody answers. What do you do with the task?
options: Complete it with a note: no answer, voicemail, payment link sent
questions.explanation: A call with no answer is a call made. Complete the task and note what you did so the next person does not repeat it.

questions.q: A caller says she found Greens by searching online. Which lead source do you pick?
questions.explanation: Pick the true source. Other is the most common source at Greens today (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026) and tells the company nothing.

questions.q: Which lead statuses does Cubby set by itself?
questions.explanation: You set New, Hot, Cold, On Hold, Unqualified and Duplicate. Cubby sets Reservation when a unit is reserved and Converted when a lease is made.

questions.q: At move-in, the customer's card is declined. What has Cubby done?
options: Kept the lease with a balance
Undone the lease and kept the lead
questions.explanation: Cubby creates the lease and then charges. If the payment is declined, the lease is rolled back and the lead survives. Never hand over a gate code first.

questions.q: A new tenant has their own insurance. How do you set coverage?
options: Own policy, with the policy number and expiration date and proof of insurance
questions.explanation: Choose the tenant's own policy (Cubby: Private Policy) and enter the number, expiration date and proof. Vehicle tenants almost all carry their own policy.

questions.q: A tenant wants to move from a 10x10 to a 10x20 at the same site. How do you do it in Cubby?
options: Move out the 10x10, then rent the 10x20
Run a transfer, which ends the old lease, starts a new one and moves the balance
Change the unit number on the lease
Add a second lease and keep both
questions.explanation: A transfer keeps the history and moves any balance between leases. A move-out plus move-in breaks both.

questions.q: How many scheduled move-outs can one lease have in Cubby?
questions.explanation: One. If the date changes, change the scheduled move-out. A task alone is not a scheduled move-out.

questions.q: A tenant locked out on the 11th pays in full at the counter. What else do you check?
options: That their gate code works and any overlock comes off
questions.explanation: Cubby changes a delinquent tenant's gate code on the 11th (what Cubby does today; under review with counsel). After payment, make sure the tenant has a working code before they leave.

questions.q: Which Greens site's gate reports its events into Cubby today?
questions.explanation: Only Fairfield's gate reports into Cubby (From Greens' Cubby, 11/2026). Its log shows Allowed, Master Code, Unknown User and Outside of Hours.

questions.q: A tenant's daughter is authorized to pay and access the unit. Where do you record it so every staff member sees it?
options: A pinned note on the tenant's contact, which shows on the lease
questions.explanation: A pinned note on the contact shows on the lease. Keep it short and current, and record that ID was checked.

questions.q: Which report shows each tenant's open charges sorted by how old they are?
questions.explanation: Aged Receivables buckets each open charge into 0-30, 30-60, 60-90, 90-120 and over 120 days.

questions.q: Which report shows what the card processor paid out to Greens' bank?
questions.explanation: Card payments are paid out in batches. Merchant Services Disbursements lists each payout so accounting can match the bank.

questions.q: At close, the cash drawer is $20.00 short of Cubby's cash payments. What do you do?
options: Edit a payment so they match
Count again, check for a payment on the wrong lease or method, and tell your manager
questions.explanation: Never change a payment to make the drawer match. Recount, look for an entry error, and tell your manager before you leave.

questions.q: What can one payment link cover?
options: Several leases for the same tenant
questions.explanation: A payment link is texted or emailed to the tenant and can cover several of their leases at once.

questions.q: Which Cubby permission lets a staff member waive a charge or issue a credit?
questions.explanation: Credits and Waives. Cubby asks no one to approve once you have it, so Greens Waivers, Credits and Refunds sets the limits.
